subject: Test for LLM anchoring (6.1) over the 63 already-paid runs
activeForm: Testing the scenarios for anchoring on the last observed value
description:
FREE. Reads the 63 runs already paid for. No new spend, no retrain, no API calls.

6.1 names four failure modes of judgmental forecasting. SCAN_LOG: 'The anchoring row is the most valuable thing in this section.'

The book: it is common to 'take the last observed value as a reference point... may lead to conservatism and undervaluing new information.'

THE TESTABLE PREDICTION: an LLM given a history and asked to forecast may anchor on the final observed value -- i.e. produce naive-1 in disguise. Measurable directly against the logged runs: compare each scenario's forecasts against the last observed value and against a naive-1 baseline.

Either result is reportable. If the plain-LLM arm anchors and the model-backed arm does not, that is a mechanism for the B->C increment rather than just a size. If nothing anchors, that is a negative result worth stating.

Ch9 material. Also pairs with 6.1's 'optimism' row and the 6.7 TFC precedent for over-forecasting in A_llm_plain.

NOTE: reads 04_SRQ4_Scenario_Experiment output but MUST NOT edit anything there -- RED zone. Write the analysis in the Branch B tree and read the run log only.
